authored.note: Explanations are written for learners. Facts are checked word for word against the cited files. The events shown in Practice are the committed specimen packs, unedited.

summary.text: A tool and a scope can both be granted and the request can still name a resource the agent may not touch. This lab shows four recorded requests against the same tool and scope, differing only in the resource named and in the profile.
facts: a granted MCP tool at a granted scope is not authorized against every resource that tool can name.

glance.label: The legitimate operation
glance.text: The agent looks up the lending-basics policy with lookup_policy at policy:read. The tool, the scope and the resource are all granted.
facts: granted `lookup_policy` at granted `policy:read` against granted resource `lending-basics`

glance.label: What the attacker controls
glance.text: The resource named in the arguments. The tool and scope are unchanged and granted; the resource exists in the catalog but is not granted.
facts: catalog-valid ungranted resource on a granted tool and granted scope

glance.label: The trust boundary
glance.text: The control reaches the resource check only after the tool and scope checks pass, so those two earlier ALLOWs do not settle the resource question.
facts: resource exists? → resource granted? → ALLOW ticket → handler.

glance.label: The authorization rule
glance.text: Arguments say which resource is wanted. They never widen what the agent is granted.
facts: Arguments identify the requested resource. Arguments do not grant authority.

glance.label: What counts as evidence of execution
glance.text: An ALLOW is a decision. The handler has begun only where a separate mcp.started event is recorded.
facts: Explain why ALLOW is not execution
Treat runtime handler count as authoritative for non-execution.

known.text: Three resource states are recorded: granted, known but ungranted, and unknown. The lab says to read the control's reason, not grant-set membership, to tell the last two apart.
facts: Do not determine known-vs-unknown from grant-set membership alone. Use the control reason.
